summary.title: A Vim Guide for Advanced Users
summary.one_liner: Learn advanced Vim features: g-prefixed keystrokes, ranges, quickfix and location lists, registers, substitute, :global, and marks.
takeaways: Use g-prefixed normal mode keystrokes such as gf, gi, gv, gn and gI to speed up editing.
Apply commands to line ranges like 1,40 or '<,'> and use quickfix and location lists to navigate errors and search results.
Use registers (named, numbered, expression) to store and reuse text, and append to macros with qA.
Use :s for substitution with flags and magic settings, and :g with :norm to run commands on matching lines.
Use marks (a-z, A-Z, 0-9) to jump to positions and use them as ranges.
summary.summary: This is the third part of a Vim series aimed at advanced users. It walks through g-prefixed normal mode keystrokes, line ranges, the quickfix and location lists, and Vim's registers, including the expression register. It then covers the substitute command with its regex "magic" modes and flags, the :global command combined with :normal, and marks. Examples are given throughout as Vim command snippets, with the author recommending practising in Vim while reading.
